content:
Creating this topic to aggregate discussion around compilation from ArkLib whether via the native compiler or custom compiler(s), as well as the verification of such compilers.

cc: @Bas Spitters @Ryan Kim @Tobias Grosser and others.

As I mentioned, I have an MLIR-inspired compiler for CT crypto similar to jasmin. I hope we can base it on VeIR.
I aligned my port of our https://github.com/AU-COBRA/AUCurves library to the dialect used by fractionalize, which were a bit more developed than the ones I came up with myself. Thanks again for the nice work @Ryan Kim
I think the easiest way to target it would be via Hax, but there are other possibilities too.

@Bas Spitters Just to clarify, do you mean you ported AUCurves to match https://github.com/fractalyze/prime-ir? Also, what exactly do you mean by targeting it via Hax? Does it mean Plonky3 will be extracted into Lean through Hax, and then become executable via an MLIR dialect built on top of VeIR? Did I understand that correctly?

@Ryan Kim I see I never sent this :see_no_evil:

Our AUCurves library for ECC in Rocq is based on fiat/bedrock/rupicola. It has a full suite of curves. For some it's the first verified implementation. I added a rust-like language for constant time compilation, and compilation targeting the verified jasmin compiler. This is a composition of two verified compilers. So we have a full tool chain (in Rocq). Working with fiat/bedrock in rocq can be very painful, so I've ported most of this to Lean.

I found it useful to structure the compiler following the standard MLIR dialects. In the process I made up some of my own, but then restructured them to fit prime-ir, because it was a very good fit with AUCurves. I've also added lattice crypto. And @Alexander Hicks suggestion to use TileIR also turned out to be a good abstract (which was the reason it was invented).
One important observation, constant time crypto is much simpler than supporting a full language.
So, at the moment this is only weakly linked to VeIR/MLIR, but I'm hoping to build on it as it matures. It's a really exciting project.
I do target VeIR from my compiler.

We can target my compiler via hax, following the methodology in Last Yard (https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/185) or directly from lean, using rupicola-like relational compilation/quoting. The latter may be easier since there is no rust code connected to arklib, yet (?).
I did some experiments with relational compilation, and it seems to work well for arklib. I have also connected arklib to CatCrypt.
So, this is one way of generalizing our Last Yard work.
